answer: Picture a mesa: trust can only climb onto it through a few narrow ramps. In a SybilRank-style graph, honest agents seed trust that flows along vouching edges, capped per edge. An attacker can spin up a thousand mirror identities, but they all hang off the few real links he controls, so they split a trickle of trust instead of multiplying it. Each new edge into the honest region costs months of earned reputation, turning his army into a fable.
